subject.title: feat: add a safe API for writing skills

question: Should OpenClaw expose a new direct and parallel skills.write public API, or limit this PR to internal consolidation while retaining the existing proposal-first Gateway contract?
rationale: The branch creates durable Gateway and potential plugin API obligations and broadens who can directly activate skill content; implementation correctness alone cannot choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow to canonical paths
options.body: Retain the internal service, use existing skills.proposals.* RPCs for proposal operations, and defer direct/plugin exposure until a separately approved contract exists.

options.title: Approve the write API
options.body: Keep the new RPC family after adding idempotency, an explicit direct-write safety gate, plugin-SDK positioning, compatibility documentation, and live proof.

options.title: Pause the consolidation
options.body: Close or substantially rework the branch if maintainers do not want a stable programmatic skill-mutation contract in core.

recommendation.title: Narrow to canonical paths
recommendation.body: Retain the internal service, use existing skills.proposals.* RPCs for proposal operations, and defer direct/plugin exposure until a separately approved contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available current-main history signal is the recent ownership of skill installation policy and safety boundaries directly affected by the new direct-write API.
